item.description:
GTA 6 developer and publisher Rockstar Games began shipping out the Grand Theft Auto VI Merch Collection on October 9, 2026. Take a look at the complete list of the available merchandise, including upcoming items available for pre-order.

Rockstar Games Now Shipping Out Vibrant Vice City-Themed Collectibles


The Grand Theft Auto VI Merch Collection Is Available for Purchase


Grand Theft Auto VI continues to drum up even more excitement among the gaming community as it speeds toward its much-awaited release. The promotional campaign has included a multi-million-dollar effort to advertise the game all over Miami City, Florida, a major deal with Netflix for its extended 26-minute gameplay showcase, massive murals, billboards, and an official playlist.

This merch line includes themed shirts, baseball caps, canvas tote bags, a money clip, a Zippo lighter, and stickers. In addition, they will be releasing a special Collector’s Box and CD and vinyl editions of the official soundtrack. The merchandise is beginning to sell out, so devoted fans may want to buy or pre-order while supplies last.

item.title: Pokémon UNITE’s End of Service Coming in 2027, and Players Are Disappointed
item.description:
Pokémon UNITE will end service in March 2027, on both Nintendo Switch and mobile. Read on to learn more about the game’s shutdown and other details here.

Pokémon UNITE Confirmed To Shut Down in March 2027


Officially Reaching End of Service


The official Pokémon UNITE account has announced that the game will end service on March 23, 2027, at 00:00 UTC (March 22 at 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET), across all platforms. The game first launched on Switch on July 21, 2021, and the team has thanked players for their support since then. After the shutdown, players will no longer be able to log in or take part in battles, and support for the game's video and image guidelines will end as well.
The wind-down has already begun, with gacha currency sales, new UNITE Club memberships, and automatic membership renewals being suspended on October 27 at 05:00 UTC. Players can keep using the Aeos gems they currently own until service ends, including current UNITE Club members who keep their benefits until their membership period runs out.

Planned Events Are Still Scheduled To Arrive


Other planned game updates will still happen. On November 12, an update is set to add a special event and a "library" feature. During the event, players can earn various items and rewards, including Unite licenses and Holowear that have appeared in the game so far. Meanwhile, the library lets players view certain records and in-game content even after the game shuts down, but only if they complete the required data download before March 23, 2027.
Library data generally cannot be transferred between devices, and support for this feature ends once the game closes. Players must accomplish the data download, or they won’t be able to view their in-game records anymore afterwards. Additionally, the Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo competitive tournament will still take place as previously announced, with qualifiers starting on December 5, 2026.

Players Express Their Frustrations


Reactions to the official announcement have been negative, with some expecting it and many players voicing frustration over the game's end. A common point raised was that the developers didn’t listen to community feedback about monetization issues and instances where bots enter matches. There were also complaints in survey responses and suggestions from both players and content creators. Several fans criticized TiMi directly, saying the game's popular IP and genre should’ve allowed it to last longer.
Others expressed sadness at the news, particularly players who had spent money on the game and enjoyed it. Some felt that the game's issues could have been addressed earlier and that the shutdown was avoidable, though some pointed to its dwindling presence in the MOBA market as another factor. For now, the official notice encourages players to keep enjoying the game until its final day.

item.title: Blue Archive JP’s Publisher Switch to Nexon in January 2027 Brings Mixed Reactions
item.description:
Blue Archive's Japanese service is changing publishers, moving from Yostar to Nexon in January 2027. Read on to learn more about the transfer announcement and other details.

Blue Archive JP Switches Publisher From Yostar to Nexon, Earning Mixed Fan Reactions


Official Statement Made During Blue Archive JP’s Latest Livestream


It was officially announced on the October 25th Blue Archive livestream that the game’s JP publisher is switching from Yostar to Nexon in January 2027. Maintenance for the switch is set for January, with the detailed schedule to be announced sometime this November. Nexon Games remains the developer, and there are no planned changes to how the game is made.
According to community summaries of the livestream, Nexon ended the contract at its request, as the full handover of publishing rights will take about three months, and previously announced offline events will continue as planned. The Chinese version, on the other hand, is reportedly staying with Yostar.

Players Must Link and Transfer Their Accounts


Nexon says all account data, including Blue Gems, packages, and items, will carry over, but players need to meet some requirements. Accounts must be first linked to a Yostar ID and registered for the transfer before the maintenance starts, while guest accounts can't be moved. After the switch, players will log in with a Nexon account instead, and anyone whose existing Nexon account was made through X (Twitter) has to register again.
Each Nexon account can hold only one Blue Archive account, so players with several Yostar IDs will need separate accounts, and Nexon Points can't be used in the game. Personal details tied to a Yostar ID, such as name and address, won't be transferred, and Nexon's own terms and privacy policy will apply. The procedure page is expected in November.
Other services are affected too. The PC version and Yostar's charge center stay available only until the maintenance begins, with Nexon preparing a new PC environment and a web-based payment option. Serial codes should be used before then, and items will keep their expiry dates. After the switch, players will receive compensation, including 100 free recruitments, and announced collaborations, merchandise, and events, including the Blue Academy Fest on January 23 and 24, are still on the way.

Japanese and Global Players Weigh In Their Worries


Reactions have been mixed, and many replies from Japanese players are those of concern. Part of the worries stem from Nexon's reputation among the community, as Nexon is focused on different marketing strategies vs. Yostar in other gacha titles, as discussed on Reddit. While Yostar is very fan-centric in promoting a game, Nexon is regarded by the gacha fans as having a heavier focus on microtransactions and monetization as leading factors. Some are hoping that the quality would not lessen or drop when going through the transition.
Though Nexon Games already serves as the core developer in JP, Yostar was widely credited with establishing Blue Archive’s media and promotional efforts and budget, especially in Japan. Fans pointed to merchandise, songs, ASMR, ads in Tokyo, the online shop, offline events, and the Blue Archive radio show, all headed by Yostar. Some players also noted that there are noticeable gaps in promotions and marketing elsewhere compared to Japan, such as fewer offline events and collaborations, less content outside the game, and past translation errors.
Several fans asked Nexon to reconsider, a few hoped Yostar would return, and some fear for the game's long-term future. Others argue the change matters less than it seems. Nexon already develops the game and publishes it everywhere outside Japan and China, so some expect just a few in-game changes, and global players describe Nexon's publishing as steady, with occasional freebies and responses to feedback. A few hope that with this, Nexon could eventually bring Japan-only extras to other regions, though that remains speculation for now.
At this time, more answers are due in November, when Nexon plans to share the maintenance schedule, the account transfer procedure, and an interview video with Blue Archive's executive producer and Yostar's CEO. Nexon confirms its commitment to updating the game's stories and features hasn't changed ahead of the sixth anniversary on February 4, 2027.

item.title: Goddess of Victory: NIKKE 4th Anniversary Welcomes Stellar Blade Collab, new Marian, and Free SSR
item.description:
Goddess of Victory: NIKKE celebrates their 4th Anniversary with a Stellar Blade collaboration, new NIKKEs to recruit, and fan events.

NIKKE’s 4th Anniversary Introduces Stellar Blade Collab, New Characters, Free SSR


Marian, Scarlet, and Rapunzel Are the 4th Anniversary Stars


As revealed in today’s livestream, Goddess of Victory: NIKKE’s 4th Anniversary celebration comes in with plenty of new content, such as a Stellar Blade music collaboration, three new characters to add to the roster, and in-person fan celebrations.
Launching on October 29th, the 4th Anniversary update introduces Marian: Queen and Scarlet: Goddeath as recruitable NIKKEs, while Rapunzel: Sanctuary is a free SSR claimable up to four times through participating in anniversary events. Various in-game rewards will be available, with Commanders (NIKKE players) earning up to 259 free recruitment attempts during the duration of the event, with 4th Anniversary NIKKE selection boxes. These special selection boxes include:
  • Rapunzel: Sanctuary
  • Chime
  • Rapunzel: Pure Grace
  • Snow White: Innocent Days

Four new costumes also make their way to the game, two of which are obtained through gacha; Marian: Queen gets a “Last Affection” wedding dress costume where she “has attained happiness with her one true love,” while Snow White: Heavy Arms receives a “Lacrimosa” costume. Battle Pass costumes, Neon_Vision and Nayuta_Vision are also available on the update’s launch.
Stellar Blade, another popular action-adventure game from SHIFT UP, makes its way to the NIKKE universe with its second collaboration in the form of a soundtrack collection. Players can enjoy 22 tracks in TRACING THE STARS x Stellar Blade, added into the game with minigame backgrounds, custom note skins, and the special character appearance.

Plus a Main Story Expansion, Story Events, and a Visual Novel Adventure


The Main Story will receive an expansion, adding Main Chapters 49-50. As the full-scale 3rd Surface Recapture War is at hand, this finale chapter marks the end of the Underground Ark plotline while also setting down the foundation for a brand-new story about to unfold. Amidst that, players can also tune into the “MARIA-n” Story Event featuring Marian in an unfamiliar environment, taking steps towards discovering long hidden secrets.
Additionally, there will be a minigame called “Fading Affection,” a choice-driven text-based visual novel with branching storylines that gives players the chance to revisit memory fragments and discover unexplored endings of the past.

Taking Over Time Square Again Alongside In-Person Fan Events


NIKKE players in New York and Los Angeles can also take part in the in-person festivities. Alongside the update launch, a special NIKKE billboard on One Times Square (1475 Broadway & 42nd St.) will be on display for the entire day of October 29th. Eager fans can see Marian in action, taking over the heart of NYC, and take pictures with her.
For those in the West Coast, NIKKE will be featured in Animate Los Angeles in a special partnership for a “dedicated anniversary experience” that will feature plenty of photo displays such as the 3D illusion wall art and NIKKE-themed store decorations. Exclusive merchandise will also be on sale, and those who would stick around for a while longer can participate in special community activities. The NIKKE x Animate LA collaboration will run from October 31st to November 14th.

Spanish Language Support To Be Added


As part of NIKKE’s “growth around the globe,” the livestream also revealed that full Spanish text localization will be added to the game on October 29th.
“We are excited to welcome more Spanish-speaking players from the LATAM region with the addition of the much requested Spanish language support launching with the 4th Anniversary Update, and we will continue to do our best to deliver exciting content for all our players going forward,” said Hyongseok Yoo, VP of SHIFT UP and NIKKE’s Game Director, suggesting that with that initiative, more localizations may be in development.

item.title: Chasing Kaleidorider Closed Beta “Doki Test” Now Open, Celebrates 2 Million Pre-Registration Milestone
item.description:
Chasing Kaleidorider is recruiting players for its next closed beta, the Doki Test, with sign-ups now open for mobile and PC. Read on to learn more about the test and other details.

Chasing Kaleidorider Gets 2M Pre-Registrations Worldwide, Doki Test Sign-Ups Available


Milestone Comes With Close Beta Applications and a Giveaway


Chasing Kaleidorider celebrates reaching 2 million global pre-registrations, and the team announced on its official X (Twitter) that Doki Test sign-ups opened on October 22. It's a closed beta with a limited player pool, and anything earned during the test, such as character progress and collected items, will be erased once it finishes instead of being kept for the full release.
Interested players can apply through a recruitment questionnaire, while regular pre-registration continues on the game's official website. The test's start and end dates haven't been revealed, so players will have to keep an eye on the official pages for updates.
The studio is also running a repost giveaway. Following the official @ChasingKaleidorider account and reposting the announcement enters players into a draw for ten $15 Amazon gift cards, with the giveaway running from October 22 to November 5. Fans have been signing up and hoping to be picked, while some asked what's new compared with the previous beta test.

How to Apply and What to Expect


The Doki Test runs on iOS, Android, and PC. On the form, applicants can choose either Android or iOS as their mobile device, and those accepted into the mobile test also receive the PC version automatically, with progress synced across both devices. The test supports five languages for text (English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese), and voiceovers only cover Japanese or Chinese.
However, applying doesn't secure a spot, since the team is only accepting a limited number of players and will go through every application. Selected players will receive an email, and they'll need to sign in with the same email they used on the form. After the recruitment period closes, the official website will also add a page where applicants can look up whether they qualified.
Other standard beta rules also apply. Handing off, selling, or sharing test access or installation files is banned, and anyone caught will lose access, with violations possibly leading to legal action. Streaming, recording, and posting screenshots are allowed, but the studio says it will take action against leaks, such as data mining the client or spreading content that hasn't been released. Since the Doki Test is a work in progress, it is important for players to note that the visuals, text, voice work, and performance could look different in the final version of the product. item.title: Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Main Trailer Introduces Norgan and New Official Pawns
item.description:
Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen received a new trailer and gameplay details during TGS 2026. Read on to learn more about Norgan, character customization, and community reactions.

Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Reveals Main Trailer and New Features


Explore the Frozen Realm of Norgan and 12 Lost Rites Dungeons on October 9


Dragon's Dogma 2 is expanding with Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen, following the premiere of the expansion's main trailer and gameplay reveals during the Capcom Spotlight: Tokyo Game Show 2026 presentation. Launching on October 9, 2026, the expansion takes the Arisen north to the long-abandoned, snow-covered realm of Norgan, where players must unravel forgotten regional tragedies and uncover how an ominous, seemingly unkillable Fallen Dragon can be slain.
The cinematic trailer showcases the harsh northern climate alongside returning franchise horrors—including the tentacled Evil Eye—and previews the 12 Lost Rites Dungeon Challenges. Functioning as the expansion's core endgame loop, these 12 multi-floor challenge gauntlets test high-level parties with escalating enemy waves, harsh environmental hazards, and boss encounters. Conquering them forms the foundation of the Relic Expedition Cycle, where players delve deep into ruins to recover and decrypt powerful unappraised gear.
To help adventurers tackle these trials, Capcom announced a new set of Official Pawns. In Dragon's Dogma, Pawns serve as AI companions summoned through the Rift to support the party. While player-created Pawns often cost Rift Crystals (RC) to hire when they exceed your level, Official Pawns are curated guest companions made in partnership with notable creators that players can hire freely without RC costs. The new roster revealed for the expansion includes VTuber Mint Fantome, popular Japanese Monster Hunter streamer 茶々茶 (Chachacha), and Yogscast creator The Spiffing Brit, giving players dedicated, pre-equipped allies built for Norgan's hazards.

Updated Character Creator and Pre-Order Bonuses


Along with the new trailer, Capcom released an update for the standalone Dragon's Dogma 2: Character Creation & Storage tool, which is now available for download across supported platforms. The tool gives players early access to upcoming customization options, including Northern-themed hairstyles and new tattoo designs, allowing Arisen to build and save their characters ahead of launch. While these new cosmetics cannot be brought into the base game immediately, saved creations will transfer directly into the expansion once it goes live.
Pre-orders are now open, with early adopters receiving the Norgan Fashion Set - Northern Attire as an exclusive cosmetic bonus.

Fans Welcome Endgame Dungeon Loop, but Voice Concerns About Enemy Variety


Fans have enthusiastically celebrated the return of the classic Dark Arisen gameplay loop—praising the addition of the 12 Lost Rites dungeons and the Relic Expedition Cycle, which many players feel evokes the beloved dungeon-crawling challenge of the original game's Bitterblack Isle. Long-requested quality-of-life adjustments, particularly the expansion of equipped skill slots from four to six, multiple save slots, and the promise of an incoming Hard Mode, have also drawn heavy praise.
However, some community members have voiced caution regarding monster variety. Discussions on forums note that several shown creatures appear to be elemental reskins of base-game enemies—such as yeti variants of the cyclops and frost drakes—prompting players to hope Capcom reveals entirely new monster skeletons and unique boss encounters prior to release.

item.title: Dispatch Anniversary Adds Behind-the-Scenes Modes, a Mobile Release, and More
item.description:
Dispatch is celebrating its first anniversary with two new playable modes, a mobile release date, and a lineup of events. Read on to learn more about the announcement, blog, and other details.

Dispatch Celebrates One Year With New Modes, Mobile Version, and Events


Over 5 Million Players Later, AdHoc Studio Adds Extra Deluxe Content


AdHoc Studio celebrated Dispatch's 1st anniversary and 5 million total players by first releasing a Deluxe Edition update that adds two behind-the-scenes modes. Cast & Crew Commentary offers over 16 hours of audio across all eight episodes, letting players pick between a cast track and a crew track in the Settings menu.
Voices include Aaron Paul, Laura Bailey, and Travis Willingham, and because the commentary changes with the choices a player makes, each playthrough can reveal something different. Storyboard Mode, on the other hand, plays the whole game with its original storyboard animatics, showing how scenes and characters looked before full production.
These are only obtainable for Digital Deluxe Edition DLC owners, which also includes the digital art book and four digital comics. However, the commentary is English-only, but the game's dialogue still shows subtitles in the chosen language. The studio's post teased what the cast might have revealed with "nothing too scandalous," and fan replies warmly thanked the team for the bonus content.

Dispatch Heads to Mobile Devices on December 9


Dispatch is also making a jump to mobile. It arrives on iOS and Android on December 9, 2026, rebuilt for touch controls and vertical play. The first four episodes will be free, so players can try the opening half of the story before deciding to continue. Unlocking the full game costs $19.99 USD, with prices varying per region.
The mobile version will be available in all regions where the PC and console versions are sold, excluding China and Japan. Pre-registration is now open on Google Play, and App Store pre-orders are listed as coming soon for now.

Physical Editions, a Live Concert, and Merch Coming


Further anniversary plans involve more offline celebrations. The physical Deluxe Edition for PS5, Xbox Series X, and Nintendo Switch 2 includes the new modes on the disc or cartridge, plus a two-sided poster, a 16-page pocket guide, and a soundtrack code. The studio is aiming to start shipping this holiday season. Meanwhile, a three-record vinyl of the soundtrack is set to ship starting in mid-November, and a hardcover making-of book called Dispatch: Design Works is planned for 2027, with pre-order details due at the end of November.
Fans interested can also go to Los Angeles to attend Night Shift, a one-night concert of the game's music at AVALON Hollywood on December 3. It's a 21+ event, with a pre-sale code going out to email subscribers on October 28, and no livestream of the event is planned.
New merch is also on sale in the studio's shop, and giveaways on Discord and the r/DispatchAdHoc subreddit are running until November 22. AdHoc’s plans to celebrate the game’s success and their fans’ support seem to be gearing up in the coming months, giving back to the community that welcomed them with open arms.
While the first-anniversary events do not include anything about a possible season 2, AdHoc Studio has previously mentioned that they were seriously considering a continuation for Dispatch after its success. These talks came immediately in November 2025, when the game reached over 1 million copies 10 days after launch.
Now that Dispatch has reached over 5 million copies sold, fans are even more hopeful about the possibility of a sequel that may just be over the horizon. For more insights on the game, feel free to check out the page below:

Gaming News At A Glance: Mass Effect Series Goes on Despite BioWare Closing, Steam Next Is Filled to the Brim With AI, Love and Deepspace Has an Ironic Collab With Blade Runner


Mass Effect Series Will Still Happen, Despite BioWare Shut Down


BioWare, the company behind three decades of legendary franchises like Baldur's Gate, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, and Mass Effect, has announced it will close on October 21. The studio also said the next Mass Effect game is ending, adding to EA's long history of disrupting development on anticipated IPs. However, there's a silver lining: the TV series in development with Amazon MGM Studios is still moving forward, and the studio hopes to replicate the success of its Fallout adaptation.

Steam Next Fest Record-Breaking 8000 Demos Are Filled With AI-Assisted Games


Steam Next Fest, an event filled with free playable demos for unreleased PC games, reached a record-breaking catalog of over 8,000 free demos, more than doubling last year's 3,000 entries. While players were able to try and wishlist anticipated games like ANOMALITH and CRYMELIGHT, the event has amassed criticism as it's flooded with AI-assisted demos or, as the players put it, "vibe-coded AI slop", causing players to beg for an option to filter it out. Some developers were so worried about the harmful effects of AI cloning their game that they held back from releasing demos, as with Drunken Goddess Reflux and ReVamp.

Love and Deepspace X Blade Runner 2049 Has Fans Thinking Whether the Developers Understood the Films


Love and Deepspace seems cursed to attract controversy after controversy ever since the Valko incident, as fans criticized their latest collaboration with Blade Runner 2049. Fans critique that their crossover PV "Love is real" showcased a severe mismatch in themes between the otome game and a film that has themes about dystopian megacorps using AI to profit off loneliness. Still, other fans are holding off on their thoughts until the collaboration drops.

New Action RPG Game Ordinary Oddness Debuts With a Trippy 22-Minute Trailer


Tencent's newest project, Ordinary Oddness, debuts with a 22-minute trailer showcasing its zany visuals and action-RPG combat rooted in urban legends. The video gives a better look into the playable character, Consulting Investigator (Investigator for brevity) of the Mythoids Investigation Agency (MIA), and takes on commissions from humans and Mythoids. Pre-registrations are now open on its official website.

Rockstar Spent Years Reinventing GTA 6's Weapon Wheel, Only to Come Back to It Anyway


As the GTA 6 release date draws near, Rockstar has been revealing more details about the anticipated game. One such detail comes from the studio's interview with Bloomberg, where it told the outlet it tried for years to replace its classic radial menu, as Rockstar wanted a loadout system more like Red Dead Redemption 2. However, after years of trying different UI and loadout systems, like webs and trays, GTA 6's final iteration is returning to the iconic weapon wheel.

Review Roundup: Oct 18th to October 24th


A Great Week for Loreheads


Loreheads and players who are into deep narratives will have a kick out of the games this week. Zenless Zone Zero released its 3.3 Journey to the Sky update with sky-high narrative highlights, while a former gacha game, Final Fantasy Resonance, is quickly becoming an instant classic after shedding off live-service aspects. Escape from Playtime is a co-op spinoff in the Poppy Playtime universe that lore theorists will spend hours dissecting. Finally, a former Capcom producer brings along company veterans for Stupid Never Dies, a roguelike co-published by SEGA.

Zenless Zone Zero 3.3 Journey to the Sky


Zenless Zone Zero’s Journey to the Sky continues the Roscaelifer storyline as the Proxies infiltrate Quietude Isle and dig further into the mysteries surrounding Sunbringer. The chapter transitions smoothly from Version 3.2, balancing an entertaining mech sequence and lighter character moments with an increasingly dire crisis and several major revelations.
Version 3.3 lands its emotional beats particularly well, giving Phoenix greater depth and making Sunbringer the chapter’s standout. Severian feels awkwardly inserted into the plot, while Carinus receives too little development for his arc to carry its intended weight. Some late developments also pass too quickly, but the story’s heart and expanding mysteries still leave us eager to see what comes next.

Final Fantasy Resonance


Final Fantasy Resonance rescues the opening storyline and cast of the discontinued mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, rebuilding them as a traditional HD-2D RPG without gacha pulls or microtransactions. Rain, Lasswell, and Fina embark on a familiar Crystal-saving adventure filled with kingdoms, airships, and other series staples, elevated by expressive pixel animation and cinematic presentation.
Its turn-based combat rewards exploiting weaknesses, staggering enemies, and building characters around Visions of familiar Final Fantasy heroes. The cast is likable, and the gameplay is rewarding, though battles can get repetitive once you understand their patterns. However, a predictable, trope-filled story, straightforward dungeons, fetch-heavy side quests, and a hesitation to take narrative risks despite teasing bigger themes still hold it back, but its early hours still deliver a satisfying old-school Final Fantasy adventure freed from its gacha roots.

Escape from Playtime


Escape from Playtime brings the familiar gather-and-extract formula of Lethal Company and R.E.P.O. into the Poppy Playtime universe. As miniature Smiling Critters, teams climb through the ruined Playtime Co. factory, solve puzzles, collect materials for an escalating quota, and evade toys like Cat-Bee, Boogie Bot, and Miss Delight. Its climbing mechanics and vertical environments give the well-worn co-op formula a welcome Playtime-flavored twist.
The Early Access build still feels underassembled, with unreliable traversal, repetitive procedural rooms, slow progression, and several poorly balanced items. Its oppressive darkness, excellent monster sound cues, and lore exploring the aftermath of the Hour of Joy are considerably stronger, offering longtime fans plenty of context and new questions to pursue. The foundations are promising, but it needs more variety, better balance, and more polish before we can fully recommend it.

item.title: Rockstar Spent Years Trying to Replace the GTA Weapon Wheel, Then Kept It for GTA 6
item.description:
Rockstar spent years testing replacements for the GTA weapon wheel before returning to it. Jason Schreier’s follow-up video shares more GTA 6 development details that missed his Bloomberg cover story.

Jason Schreier Shares GTA 6 Development Details Left Out of His Bloomberg Cover Story


Rockstar Returned to the Weapon Wheel After Years of Testing Alternatives


Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) keeps the classic weapon wheel after Rockstar Games spent months, if not years, trying to replace it. The studio wanted a more restrictive loadout system, and the team ended up back at the wheel anyway.
The weapon wheel is the radial menu that lets players pause the action and pick a weapon from their collection. In GTA 5, it gives quick access to an entire arsenal, so a player can switch from a pistol to a rocket launcher in a couple of button presses.
The detail comes from a video by Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier, who covered material from his interviews at Rockstar North in Edinburgh that did not make it into his Bloomberg Businessweek cover story on GTA 6’s development, published on October 14, 2026. He says Rob Nelson, one of Rockstar’s heads of development, shared the story with him.
According to Schreier, Nelson explained that the team wanted GTA 6’s weapon system to work more like Red Dead Redemption 2’s. Players would have to choose a loadout and hold a limited number of weapons at a time, so pulling out a rocket launcher alongside a full set of other guns would no longer be possible.
The wheel itself raised concerns, as the team worried over the fact that a weapon wheel with so few weapons would show many blank spots, reminding players of everything they couldn’t carry. That idea led Rockstar to look for something else.
He says the team spent months, if not years, on the search. They tried trays, webs, and other UI concepts, and they also tried removing the wheel altogether. After all that iteration, the final game still ended up a weapon wheel.
Schreier says anyone in game development will recognize the outcome as "that’s game development," where intense iteration can end back at the original idea. He adds that this can frustrate the people doing the UI work and prototyping. He ties the episode to the difficult stretch in the game’s development, which he says ended around late 2022 to early 2023 as the game began coming together.

GTA 6’s Map Took Over 11 Years of Work and Has Narrower Roads


The weapon wheel was only one of many long-running decisions. Schreier says planning began in 2015, when the team made its first research trip to Miami, and some artists have worked on it for more than 11 years. Bloomberg’s report also notes that the project carried the internal name Project Americas.
Art director Aaron Garbett explained that GTA 6 uses far narrower roads than GTA 5, whose wide streets felt closer to a racing game. The team made that decision from the start, and it rippled through the whole map. Garbett told Schreier, "All these things sort of come to bite you later." Denser traffic and tighter streets meant the team had to build denser buildings and environments around them, which gives the city its more realistic urban feel.

Rockstar’s Miami Research Trips Included Police Ride-Alongs and Aerial Photography


Real-world research shaped that urban feel. The team made extensive trips to Miami, including police ride-alongs and visits to places Rockstar developers described as scary. At one point, artists in a helicopter taking aerial photos of the city accidentally hovered over a Beyoncé concert.
During fieldwork, the team met many colorful characters in Miami. Jonathan Ashcroft, Rockstar’s senior vice president of technology, told him, "As soon as they know where you’re from, they just want to tell you every crime they or their friends have ever done." Those stories suit a game that encourages more robberies than ever before.

The 2019 to 2022 Period Left Rockstar Struggling to Balance Realism and Arcade Gameplay


Back at the studio, balancing realism against GTA’s traditional pace proved harder than the research. Schreier shared that the team spent 2019 to 2022 trying to merge Red Dead Redemption 2’s immersive systems with the more arcade-style feel of a GTA game. Many people felt the game was treading water, and the indecision, along with the idea of having “too many cooks in the kitchen” among three heads of development, led to frustration and tension. Some designers left as a result.
Red Dead 2 also supplied some of the ideas the team was weighing. He recounts a story from Nelson about an early prototype that Mark Tennant, Rockstar’s vice president of animation, built for Red Dead 2 around 2014 or 2015. It lets players press L2 to greet or antagonize NPCs instead of only pointing a weapon at them.
Phil Hooker, another head of development, was reluctant to show it to Nelson at first because Nelson is known for wanting to do everything. Nelson told the Bloomberg journalist, “This is incredible. This will revolutionize the way our games and our worlds work.” That prototype led to the interaction system players see in Red Dead 2. As of writing, Schreier is unsure whether GTA 6 has a deeper version of it.

Rockstar’s Art Production Team Grew From 5-6 People to 65


Managing that creative tension took more structure as the studio grew. Bloomberg’s reporting puts Rockstar at 4,711 employees across 12 offices in 2026, up from 2,441 in 2018. Schreier’s video adds a closer look at how production changed. Garbett told him the art production team went from five or six people on GTA 5 to 65 for GTA 6.
Producers manage schedules with graphs and metrics that help estimate how long tasks will take, adding a layer of bureaucracy that contrasts with the studio’s more organic past.

Rockstar Still Lets Developers Add Their Own Hidden Details


Even with that structure, Schreier says Rockstar protects individual autonomy. Garbett told him, "There’s no one person that has this whole thing in their head." Developers are given a little autonomy to add details and features they think are cool.
Garbett’s example was the famous Red Dead Redemption 2 detail where horses’ testicles shrink or expand with the weather. It was not originally on the list of features to make, and someone chose to add it on their own because they thought it was a cool detail and had the time. His point is that players will likely discover features even Rockstar’s top developers do not know about, and that culture is part of what makes the studio’s worlds feel so detailed.
Schreier’s extra notes show a studio that spent more than a decade refining a single map while testing bold ideas, discarding some, and keeping others. The weapon wheel’s return captures that process well. After months of experiments, Rockstar chose the design that worked best. Fans who want to see how these systems come together can check our coverage of the extended look with 26 minutes of new gameplay.
Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar’s official summary says the story follows Jason and Lucia, whose easy job goes wrong and pulls them into a criminal conspiracy across the fictional state of Leonida. We have also covered how Jason and Lucia took 8 years of work to make their relationship possible. The launch date has already affected other releases, with developers saying GTA 6 caused the Danganronpa 2x2 delay.
Sources:

item.title: Mass Effect Game Canceled as EA Shuts Down BioWare, But TV Series Will Still Push Through
item.description:
EA has shut down BioWare and ended development on the next Mass Effect game, though Prime Video's live-action series is reportedly still in development. Read on to learn more about the studio closure, the TV series update, and other details.

EA Shuts Down BioWare and Cancels the Next Mass Effect, But TV Series Remains in Development


BioWare Announces Its Closure After More Than 30 Years


BioWare announced its closure on X (Twitter) on October 21, ending the studio behind Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect, and Anthem. The statement confirmed that early development on the next Mass Effect project is also ending, with the studio focusing on supporting its team through the transition. It does not address what will happen to the franchises themselves.
Amid the news, IGN reported, citing sources inside Prime Video, that the Mass Effect television series remains in development at Amazon MGM Studios. All of the creatives attached to the project are said to still be on board, including showrunner Doug Jung (Mindhunter), writer Daniel Casey (Fast and Furious 9), executive producer Karim Zreik, and former Marvel Studios executive Ari Arad.

Sparked Discussions on Factors Surrounding the Franchise


The game series has been in development at Prime Video since 2024 and is set after the events of the original game trilogy. The production team had previously eyed a Q4 2026 production start, though the show still has no release date. Prime Video is also reportedly hoping to replicate the success of its Fallout adaptation, while Casey denied reports in April that the studio had asked for rewrites to make the show more appealing to non-gaming audiences.
BioWare's closure, however, also reignited discussions around EA's history with the studios it has acquired. Fans pointed to a Reddit thread listing past closures such as Bullfrog, Westwood, Origin, and Pandemic, with some commenters criticizing publisher pressure and trend-chasing as contributing factors. Others are instead looking forward to sci-fi RPGs like Exodus, which one commenter noted is being made by Archetype Entertainment, a studio run by some of BioWare's former Mass Effect developers.

item.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) Launches October 22 With Cyberware Customization and Dual-Wielding
item.description:
Cyberpunk 2077 is getting a free Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) on October 22, with a REDstreams broadcast set to share more information. Read on to learn more about the update announcement and other details.

Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) Available on October 22


Update Adds Cyberware Customization and Dual-Wielding, REDstreams Set for October 21


CD Projekt Red has announced a new free update for Cyberpunk 2077, Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5), which is scheduled to arrive on October 22, 2026. The studio revealed it on October 20 through the game's official X (Twitter) account and a post on the official website, arriving alongside the launch of the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 anime. The update will be available on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and the Nintendo Switch 2.
The studio conducted a REDstreams broadcast on October 21 at 5 PM CEST (8 AM PT / 11 AM ET), offering a closer look at some of the new features, and it is available on the following platforms: Twitch, YouTube, and Steam. CD Projekt Red has confirmed that Update 2.5 will introduce new cyberware customization and a new dual-wielding gameplay. A teaser poster features Edgerunner 2’s Weak Kingsley and a male V sporting 2 firearms, highlighting the new dual-wielding style.

Features Overview and Patch Notes Released


CD Projekt Red has released the official patch notes and a Features Overview video for Update 2.5. The dual-wielding playstyle comes from a new Double Trouble perk in the Cool skill tree, backed by four auxiliary perks, which now lets players dual-wield Power pistols and revolvers. Cyberware customization lets players visit one of five Glamdocs to give their Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire, or Projectile Launch System new skins with custom colors.
The update additionally includes a side quest called Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, which rewards a five-piece gear set based on the character King, plus a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring tracks from the anime. Cross-platform mod support through mod.io is also available across all platforms.

Another Edgerunners Update for Night City


This is not the first time the game has marked an Edgerunners release with a free update. Patch 1.6, also known as the first Edgerunners Update, arrived on September 6, 2022, a week before the first anime premiered on Netflix on September 13.
The main addition was Wardrobe, a Transmog feature that lets players change an outfit's look without affecting armor stats, including new gigs, new weapons, and cross-platform progression. The patch also had Edgerunners easter eggs across Night City, including new equipment and Photo Mode features, which led players to items like David Martinez's jacket and Rebecca's shotgun, Guts. Version 1.6 also introduced character customization at Ripperdocs, which makes cyberware customization a natural next step.
Despite Cyberpunk 2077’s rocky start, the effort to keep its momentum going hasn’t gone unnoticed by the gaming community. As one of the revolutionary titles in the industry, it’s a part of the few that’s managed to go from negative reviews to being highly acclaimed, deserving of recognition thanks to its overhauls and major updates like this.

item.title: Dead by Daylight's Diablo Collection Brings Lilith, Belial, and Mephisto to the Fog
item.description:
Dead by Daylight's Diablo Collection is headlining its month-long October of Horror, bringing six skins from the three-decade-long franchise. Find out more details about which villains and classes made the final cut.

Dead by Daylight Opens the Gates of Hell With Six-Outfit Diablo Crossover on October 20


Lilith, Belial and Mephisto Lead a Six-Outfit Collection


Dead by Daylight is bringing Sanctuary’s demons with a six-outfit Diablo collection scheduled for October 20. Developer Behaviour Interactive first revealed the collaboration during the game’s tenth-anniversary celebrations in June, then teased its arrival with a post on X (Twitter) on October 19.
The collection turns the Killers side into Diablo villains: The Artist becomes Lilith, The Dredge becomes Belial, and The Nurse takes on Mephisto’s appearance. Notably, Lilith is a Visceral outfit with unique menu animations and a custom Mori (special execution). In a separate X post on October 21, the studio confirms that that the Diablo 4 voice actors Caroline Faber, Steve Blum, and Ray Porter reprise their roles as Lilith, Mephisto, and Belial, respectively.
For the survivors, their cosmetics represent Diablo 4’s playable classes: Zarina Kassir receives a Sorceress outfit, David King becomes a Barbarian, and Taurie Cain takes on the Necromancer look. Both collections are visual transformations for existing characters, not a full Chapter, so they don't add Diablo class abilities or introduce the Prime Evils as separate Killers with original powers.
The Diablo Collection is the headline release in Dead by Daylight’s wider October of Horror lineup, a month-long Halloween rollout spanning new cosmetics, crossovers, and a seasonal event. After the game’s divisive Alien-inspired September update that brought the Xenomorph Queen into DBD’s 2v8 game mode, Behaviour Interactive looks to turn things around with this latest crossover. It began on October 1 with Hallowed Blight outfits for Jason Voorhees, The Houndmaster, and The Knight, giving Jason his first Blighted appearance since he joined the game in June.
On October 6, the NieR:Automata Collection followed, introducing Legendary 2B and A2 outfits for Feng Min and Yui Kimura, along with an Emil-inspired look for The Legion. Additionally, the Stranger Things characters Vecna, Nancy, and Steve are getting alternate costumes and a themed mode.

Fans Praise Lilith, But Wanted a Full Diablo Chapter


Fans on social media like X and Reddit have a lukewarm reception to the collection, with The Artist as Lilith the only standout addition. However, fans are mostly disappointed with her accompanying Mori, calling it anticlimactic because the elaborate buildup of her execution ends with her simply stabbing the Survivor with the spikes on her wings. Meanwhile, The Dredge as Belial received some praise for its design, but its biggest criticism is that the skin makes the character unrecognizable to both franchises, as fans couldn’t recognize the Killer or immediately associate it with Diablo.
Mephisto has received the most polarizing response of the three, as its critics are less convinced by how the Lord of Hatred has been adapted to The Nurse. Her hunched, floating posture can make his body look awkwardly draped over the existing character, making her look asleep on the job. Additionally, Mephisto’s extra arms seem to add little to her animations.
Meanwhile, the Survivors have been discussed less because they lack recognizable personalities. The decision to theme their skins around classes rather than specific Diablo characters makes them feel more like generic fantasy outfits, especially since the game already has similar medieval and fantasy-themed cosmetics. Fans suggested possible characters from the three-decade-long franchise, including the iconic Deckard Cain, Diablo 3 companion Leah, original protagonist Prince Aidan, and the Angel of Justice Tyrael.
Beyond the individual designs, a recurring disappointment is that Diablo received a cosmetic collection rather than a complete Chapter. As other players pointed out, a full Diablo Chapter could have given someone like Diablo, Baal, or the often-requested Butcher an original power and perks instead of applying their appearance to an existing Killer. Chapters also usually include a new map, and Dead by Daylight fans were hoping for one based on Diablo’s New Tristam or some sort of early teaser for the upcoming Diablo 5.

Pocketpair has just teased Palworld: Side by Side, the game's next update. Read on to find out more on the announcement and other details so far.

Palworld: Side by Side Update Set for Winter 2026


Teaser Hints at Popular Characters Zoe, Auri, and Saya


Palworld developer Pocketpair has announced Palworld: Side by Side, the survival game's next update, which is scheduled to release in Winter 2026. The announcement came on October 20 alongside the results of the Palworld Global Popularity Poll 2026. Pocketpair has yet to reveal specific details about the upcoming update or announce an exact release date, though its teaser image gives a hint at what players can expect.

However, the developer has not explicitly stated whether these characters will receive new content in the update. The poll included almost all Pals and in-game characters, with Sekhmet taking first place in the Pal category in the global results.
The community was also quick to point out that the mystery figures align with three of the game’s iconic tower bosses. Fans Excited for the Latest Update

item.title: New Open-World RPG Ordinary Oddness Releases 22-Minute Reveal Trailer as First Announcement
item.description:
Ordinary Oddness, a new “Nothing-Stays-Oddinary Open-World RPG” from Tencent, reveals a 22-minute announcement trailer.

Ordinary Oddness Welcomes Players to Elysian Skies


“Nothing-Stays-Oddinary” Open-World RPG


Tencent reveals their newest title, Ordinary Oddness, a “Nothing-Stays-Oddinary” open-world RPG through a 22-minute reveal trailer showcasing its whimsical world and action-packed gameplay. In Ordinary Oddness, logic is suspended and urban legends and fantasy creatures known as Mythoids come to life in the city of Elysian Skies—”strange is simply common sense.” While a release date has yet to be announced, pre-registrations are now open on its official website.
Players take on the role of a Consulting Investigator (Investigator for brevity) of the Mythoids Investigation Agency (MIA) and take on commissions from humans and Mythoids. It begins mundane and ordinary, but there is nothing truly ordinary in Elysian Skies as the hidden secrets and the darkness seep out from the shadows, painting that not everything is as good as it seems to be.
The trailer is a sneak peek into the one of the many chapters or “case files” of the game’s main story, and it opens to what appears to be a promotional video narrated by a flamboyant individual with a hand for a head named Yeahman showing the glitz and glamour of Elysian Skies, “the greatest city ever.” The Mythoid Day celebration, a day commemorating the peaceful coexistence of humankind and the Mythoids, is coming up soon. But of course, not everything is as it seems. The festivities are stopped by a villainous girl named Luminar, who turned almost all of the citizens into giant gummy people through candy she managed to distribute—and someone who seems to have some sort of history with the mysterious protagonist, deeper than just mere friends.

Layered Combat Makes Battles More Engaging


Ordinary Oddness said in their official website that the game “focuses on rethinking how combat mechanics interact, delivering a dynamic system built around player choice.” The player’s combat style is made up of seamless action sequences, chained together using blocks, dodges, the switching of characters, and QTEs. Relative to that, bosses and enemies also have their own unique combat styles, all of them tied to their personal storyline and appearance, creating a battlefield with ever-shifting rules. Players must learn to adapt on the fly.
In the trailer, we see the Investigator and his team battle against a boss called Annie and Her Friends, taking in perfectly-timed blocks, dodges, and skills to take down foes. Gamers familiar with games like Genshin Impact, Wuthering Waves, Silver Palace, Arknights: Endfield, and the like, will find themselves familiar with its combat to a degree and may feel right at home, although Ordinary Oddness appears to have more of a focus on action than their contemporaries. Later on, he also takes on The Nightingale Girls in another thrilling snippet of battle.

The Consulting Investigator Was a Past Criminal


The trailer dives a little deeper than a usual introduction to a new game, showcasing not only visuals, exploration mechanics, and its combat system, but also places the lore in center stage, already planting the seeds for theorists and sleuths to piece together. Ten minutes in, the connection between Luminar and the protagonist is revealed, albeit in a vague manner. They were both victims of the Nightingale Theater incident, and were close enough (or, perhaps blood-related) for Luminar to call him “Big Brother.” The idea of being a criminal or something adjacent to it also stems from Luminar calling him accusing him of leaving “this” life behind and having “gone legit,” turning into the lapdog of someone named Goodman.
And the most incriminating detail—”But who remembers that the so-called victim…was actually the one behind the massacre?” It is also odd that Luminar says, word for word, that the Investigator is the “only survivor” of the incident, yet here she is in flesh, and so is Arabella, who has also been noted as a victim. They are both alive and well—but in a world where nothing is ordinary and almost anything can happen, their existence is an anomaly in itself.
After chasing Luminar down a reimagined anomaly reminiscent of the Nightingale Theater, he finally manages to defeat her in one final showdown, or what was supposedly the final showdown. Luminar turns the tables at the end, immobilizing the Investigator and seemed to have taken the victory. However, one sentence—”Let go of me”—shatters the dream-like sequence and snaps him back to reality, to what appears to be the beginning of the Mythoid Day celebrations. The trailer concludes with a doll version of Luminar, further muddling the waters and leaving eager players with a cliffhanger.

Ordinary Oddness EN

item.title: Steam Next Fest Is Bigger Than Ever, But Players Are Asking For An AI Filter
item.description:
Steam Next Fest: October 2026 Edition features many demos, and players worry AI-generated content is making hidden gems even harder to find. Read on to learn more about the Steam event, community reaction, and other details here.

Steam Next Fest Features 8,000 Demos, and Players Say AI Is Burying the Original Ones


Steam Next Fest Doubles Its Demo Amount From Last Year


Steam Next Fest began on October 19th with more than 8,000 demos at launch, and that number has raised concerns for both creators and consumers. Steam's official X (Twitter) announced that the event runs until October 26, though many comments have raised complaints about AI-related games.
The number of demos has sparked issues among the community about AI-generated content. Valve has required AI disclosure since 2024, but players still have no way to filter out AI-tagged games, and at least a fifth of this batch’s demos carry a generative AI disclosure, with real usage potentially even higher.

Players Say Non-AI Demos Are More Difficult to Find


Comments were filled with requests for an AI filter or a store preference to hide generative AI content, similar to the existing mature content setting. Several players said the volume made it hard to find worthwhile demos, with one user claiming about 80 percent of what they were seeing was AI-made on their Steam account.
Others described much of the lineup as “vibe-coded” or stolen and warned that real effort was being buried underneath it. A few fans said the best part of Next Fest is still discovering hidden gems, but with the amount to get through, it’s proving more challenging than expected.

Bucky Argues That Next Fest Has Always Been a Gamble


Palworld's John "Bucky" Buckley weighed in on X (Twitter), contrasting the idea that the flood of demos is the main reason games go unnoticed. In his view, a large share of Next Fest entries has always gone nearly unseen, even before generative AI.
Steam's heavy shuffling of early visibility rarely changes that once the first day passes, when attention tends to gather around a couple dozen standouts. He added that the audience has likely grown, with streamers and a wider appetite for smaller games bringing in newer players who gravitate to the biggest demos, leaving the smaller entries likely to have minimal visibility.
He acknowledged that standing out is getting harder and that "AI slop" is a real problem, but he urged developers not to pin all the blame on it. He also cited the How To Market A Game analysis, with reports showing that the number of wishlists gained in June 2024 per game was still similar to how many wishlists were earned in February 2026. According to Bucky, Next Fest remains a "gamble" that is still "worth taking".

Developers Pull Back Public Demos Over Cloning Fears


Separate from the visibility issue, some developers are limiting who gets to try their games. One example is when Alliance Arts said on October 16 that Drunken Goddess Reflux will no longer do the public demo originally slated for October 19. Instead, a limited set of closed online sessions will take its place.
The team gave two explanations: its current staff cannot realistically police or moderate all the rules on posting and streaming that it had planned for a public release, but they’re also worried the demo's contents might be used instead to "imitate or replicate the game's presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools."
Players who want in must now apply through the official Discord and accept the participation rules first. Responses were mostly sympathetic, given the ongoing issues with content being stolen or copied.
Digital Sun, the studio behind Moonlighter, took a similar step on October 19, scaling ReVamp's first playtest down to a Discord-based test and pushing the public version back. The studio pointed to recent reports of unreleased games being copied and put on sale before the originals could ship and said a wide public build felt like "too big a risk." Discord testing begins on October 29, with a public playtest hoped for around January.
Since demos are one of the main ways indie games gather traction and wishlists, the frustration of developers and the contingencies they must take to protect their projects are understandable. This trend shows how far AI's reach extends, affecting both the people looking for new games to try and the teams creating them.

The second week of October brings news about this year's highly-anticipated games. Phantom Blade Zero's 66-Day difficulty mode stumps even its own developers, the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake introduces something new for players, and GTA 6 will have a shot at The Game Awards, entering eligibility by one day. The CN-strong Naruto mobile comes to global, and we were able to sit down with the developers of Truckful about their new cozy-horror delivery game.
Here’s a quick look at some of the week’s biggest gaming headlines.

Gaming News At A Glance: SummaryOfMostInterestingTitles


Phantom Blade Zero’s 66-Day Mode Is So Hard Even the Devs Can’t Beat It Without Dying


Phantom Blade Zero’s hardest mode, 66 Days, is the ultimate challenge—so much so that even the developers themselves can’t beat the game without dying, shared S-GAME Director Qiwei “Soulframe” Liang. That is thanks to the game’s focus on “behavioral complexity,” where the boss AI’s system is designed to emulate a real human player in PvP, as they wanted to provide that experience or “feeling of fighting a living person.” Each unique boss will require a different strategy, allowing players more immersion and action.
We were also able to try out the game in a hands-on preview.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Will Now Let You Pummel Bosses in a Rematch


The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake will introduce the Hall of Fallen Foes, an arena-like new area where players can take previously defeated bosses down with a rematch in timed challenges. Revealed through an overview trailer posted on October 14th, it showed an example of the new game “mode” through King Dodongo

NARUTO Mobile Finally Arrives on Global After a Decade


NARUTO Mobile is now set to arrive globally sometime between 2027 and 2029, as revealed at the Naruto panel at the October 10th New York Comic Con. A release date or window has yet to be revealed. The game’s global launch is part of the three-year Project Rasengan initiative, a multi-year plan for the franchise.
The gacha-style fighting game has long topped revenue lists despite being a China-exclusive that first released back in May of 2016, consistently garnering at least $19 million USD monthly despite being only in one region.

GTA 6 The Game Awards Eligibility Paints An Award Sweep For the Game


GTA 6 dropped a new launch trailer and is officially qualified for The Game Awards, managing to beat the deadline by just one day. To be eligible for the awards ceremony, a title must be commercially available by Friday, November 20, 9PM PT—and GTA 6 is launching on November 19th.
Fans are expecting a GTA 6 domination, considering how highly anticipated the game is. Other gamers, though, are frustrated at the prospect, arguing that there is already an expectation for its win, not when there are plenty of other games released in 2026 that deserve an award.

Truckful is A Cozy-Horror Title That Brings You to The Countryside


Truckful is the “Dredge on wheels” you never knew you needed. The cozy puzzle-mystery title by Poland-based developer MythicOwl to deliver players the “idyllic side of rural life” as a courier placed in the middle of nowhere, in a village that is bright on the outside, but there lies hidden dangers. The hand-painted visuals inspired by Studio Ghibli, Gravity Falls, and the Polish countryside may bring about a sense of comfort, but it surprises you in other ways.
It’s more than just a “wacky physics game”—it has story, colorful characters, a large world to explore, and much to learn. It prides itself on providing an experience: "”Does what I'm seeing while creating this properly convey the feelings I had when experiencing beautiful views, films, and games?” the developers shared.

To Launch on September 15th

While there is no official announcement yet on any of Aniimo’s social media accounts as of writing, the PlayStation Store front clearly notes that it will be releasing simultaneously in all regions on September 15th or 16th, depending on location, with the bottom description also writing that "Aniimo will officially launch as a free-to-play title on September 16, 2026 at 10:00 (UTC+8). item.title: Aniimo Spotlights Unique Creature Design and Hand-Drawn Animations Each in Behind-The-Scenes Showcase
item.description:
Aniimo developer Pawprint Studio shared new details on the creative vision behind the upcoming open-world RPG. Learn more about the design process for the continent of Idyll and how fans are reacting to the new developer showcase.

Aniimo Developer Details the Creation of Idyll in Behind-the-Scenes Showcase


Pawprint Studio Explores the Journey From Concept to Reality


Aniimo developer Pawprint Studio has released an official behind-the-scenes documentary, giving players a closer look at the creative endeavor required to bring the upcoming free-to-play, next-gen creature-catching action RPG to life ahead of its September 16th launch.
The showcase highlights the development team's journey of turning abstract concepts into the continent of Idyll. Focusing heavily on world-building and creature design, the documentary emphasizes the studio's goal to make every creature feel integrated into a living environment where players can forge new bonds. Behind-the-scenes clips reveal contributions across different departments, including environment design, character modeling, and animation, with animators noting that each creature features a massive suite of hand-keyframed animations to ensure high fidelity.

Hand-Crafted Creature Animations Take Center Stage


A major highlight of the video is the deep dive into the painstaking effort required to bring the world's wildlife to life. Highlighting the massive scale of production behind the project, Tengfei, a model designer, explained that materials used for Aniimo still follow real-world laws of physics, but are refined, elevated, and reimagined for the game. He stated, "Take the Nimbi for example. A real sheep might have realistic fur or curly wool. But the Nimbi incorporates the characteristics of clouds, so we need to blend wool-like and cloud-like materials."
The development team also noted that creatures are designed around their distinct body features and natural personality traits rather than solely focusing on conventional cuteness. This approach shines through in playful additions like Nimbi, a fluffy teal-peach cloud creature, and Reefish, the quirky aquatic Aniimo with a blobfish-like design. They stand alongside other standout roster entries like Bouldus, the rugged rock-rolling Aniimo; Magmarex, the imposing fiery reptilian brute; and the graceful butterfly Aniimo, Gracewing.
Each and every Aniimo is made with care, down to its unique, handmade animations. Animator Lu Kun shared that "all of them [the animations] are manually keyframed," despite the massive effort it would take. Each individual Aniimo has about at least 100 animations, all tailored to that specific creature—"we never reuse animations across different Aniimo," he clarified.
Ayu, another co-animator, added that the team considered using motion capture for efficiency but ultimately decided against it in favor of creating a fun, imaginative world.
"Why do we put in so much effort? Why spend so much time on things that might seem they're not worth the trouble? There's only one goal: to create this world. To make it feel more alive and authentic. That's a world that truly feels like it's living and breathing," she concluded.

Fans Appreciate Developer Transparency and Teased Creatures


The behind-the-scenes video has sparked positive engagement across community hubs like Reddit and X. Fans have expressed genuine appreciation for seeing the real people behind the project, noting that transparent developer insights build strong confidence ahead of launch.
Additionally, community discussions quickly zeroed in on the highlighted creature concepts featured in the video, with fan favorites like Reefish and Nimbi quickly generating widespread excitement among creature-collector veterans.

item.title: Aniimo Hits 160k Concurrent Players on Steam, Also Now Available on Mobile
item.description:
Aniimo surpasses 160,000 peak concurrent Steam players as its mobile version officially launches worldwide.

Aniimo Surpasses 160K Steam Players Alongside Mobile Launch’s Debut


Landed in Steam's Global Top 10 Sellers Chart


Aniimo, an open-world monster-collecting RPG by Pawprint Interactive Entertainment, has broken onto Steam's Global Top Sellers chart afterits mobile version officially launched on September 23, 2026, following its PC and console debut the week prior. According to SteamDB, concurrent players have climbed past 168,000, continuing a streak of daily records since its release on September 16.
To highlight the milestone, the developers sent players a Sparkling Egg reward, which has a Sparkling variant Aniimo, to their in-game mailbox as a thank-you, with more celebrations teased for the future.
In Aniimo, players get to explore the continent of Idyll while capturing and raising over 200 different creatures called Aniimo. The core mechanic lets players "twin" with their Animo to borrow their abilities for traversal, puzzle-solving, combat, and more. The mobile version carries over the same features as its PC and console counterparts, with full cross-play and cross-save support across all platforms.

Mobile Gets Slight Delays with Players Being Compensated


The mobile release did hit a short delay, lasting roughly less than an hour, as Aniimo's official X (Twitter) account announced that service would be pushed back to ensure the quality of the update. Servers eventually went live shortly after, and the team confirmed a compensation package of 1000 Glimmers, the game’s premium currency, a total of the original maintenance and the added delay, along with a Sparkling Cube, for catching Aniimo.
Since the in-game mailbox was temporarily unavailable at the time, the developers said the rewards would arrive in two separate mails once said function was restored.
Aniimo is free-to-play with in-game purchases and is available now on PC via Steam and Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, iOS, and Android. For more insights on the game, check out the article below!
